The 2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Kentucky will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the six U.S. representatives from the state of Kentucky, one from each of the state's congressional districts. The elections will coincide with other elections to the House of Representatives, elections to the United States Senate, and various state and local elections. The primary elections took place on May 19, 2026.[1]

2026 Kentucky's 4th congressional district election
← 2024
2028 →
 
Nominee Ed Gallrein Melissa Strange
Party Republican Democratic
Incumbent U.S. representative

Thomas Massie
Republican



See also: Kentucky's 4th congressional district

The 4th district is located in the northeastern part of the state, along the Ohio River, including the suburbs of Cincinnati and the eastern suburbs of Louisville. The incumbent is Republican Thomas Massie, who was re-elected unopposed in 2024.[2]

Republican primary

[edit | edit source]

Thomas Massie, a libertarian Republican first elected in 2012, has frequently clashed with Donald Trump on fiscal and international issues both during and between his terms as president.[32][33] By March 2025, Trump had openly called for a primary challenge to Massie in response to his votes on the 2025 federal budget.[34] Other high-profile clashes between the two have included Massie's vote against the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, his advocacy for the release of the Epstein files, and his condemnation of U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear sites.[35][36]

On October 17, 2025, Trump endorsed farmer and retired Navy SEAL Ed Gallrein for the seat.[37] On October 21, Gallrein announced his candidacy, challenging Massie.[38] On May 11, 2026, the primary became the most expensive U.S. House primary in American history, with over $25.6 million in ad spending beating the prior record of $25.2 million from the Democratic primary for New York's 16th congressional district in 2024.[39] By May 17, ad spending exceeded $32 million, with pro-Israel interest groups accounting for over $9 million of the spending against Massie.[40] Massie described the primary election as a "referendum on whether Israel gets to buy seats in Congress,"[41] while others described it as a referendum on Trump.[42]

During the campaign, pro-Massie and pro-Gallrein PACs both used AI-generated political ads to attack each other's campaigns.[43][44] One AI-generated ad from pro-Gallrein PAC MAGA KY included imagery of Massie having a threesome with pro-Palestinian Democratic representatives Ilhan Omar and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.[45] Massie, Omar, and former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene condemned the ad, with Greene accusing the ad of violating the TAKE IT DOWN Act.[45] On May 16, a pro-Trump group announced that Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth would visit Kentucky to raise support for Gallrein. Hegseth's move was accused by critics of violating the Hatch Act, which the White House denied.[46] During the campaign, Gallrein declined to debate Massie, ignored most interview requests, and conducted few public rallies.[47][48][49]

On May 19, Gallrein obtained the Republican nomination, defeating Massie 54.9% to 45.1%. Massie conceded the election on election night, joking in his concession speech that "it took a while to find Ed Gallrein in Tel Aviv."[50] AIPAC later sent out an announcement on X, stating that "support for America's alliance with Israel is good policy and good politics."[51]
